examples.explanation: Keeping one of each of 'a', 'b' and 'c' allows "abc", "bac" or "bca"; "abc" is the smallest of these.
The distinct letters are 'a', 'b', 'c' and 'd', and "acdb" is the smallest ordering obtainable as a subsequence.
"abc" can be formed (for instance from positions 0, 1 and 4) and no smaller arrangement of 'a', 'b', 'c' is a subsequence.

hints: Record the last position of every letter so you know whether a stacked character can still appear later.
Scan once with a monotonic stack: pop a larger top character that is still unused and occurs again ahead before pushing the current one.
Track which letters are already in the stack to skip repeats.
title: 405. Remove Duplicate Letters
